assumptions: At least one narrowly defined installation or mobile-service trade has material proof-to-invoice friction that the cited general-purpose products do not solve.
The family installation company may opt in to a lawful pilot without employer resources, confidential data, or implied production authorization.
Necessary taxpayer permissions, data-processing terms, and accounting integration rights can be obtained on commercially acceptable but nonexclusive terms.
A one-trade, export-first pilot can be built and supported within the founder's five-hour daily limit and available capital; broad multi-package production coverage cannot initially be assumed.
The proposed path to substantial founder equity requires premium willingness to pay, durable retention, and scalable partner distribution, none of which is established by the packet.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Run target-trade pilots that measure current rekeying time, rejection and reconciliation rates, days-to-invoice, and support burden; obtain paid commitments at the proposed price; demonstrate a materially better proof-to-reconciled-invoice outcome than the Ministry app, inFakt, and Comarch; and secure at least one repeatable accounting-office or field-software channel with measured CAC, activation, contribution margin, and retention.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The mandatory KSeF transition creates a coherent opportunity to remove a field-to-office handoff and make invoice completion measurable. However, stable production operation and existing official and incumbent offline-mobile workflows show that the regulation-to-field mismatch is not itself a distinctive insight; the narrower job-evidence and reconciliation gap remains unproved.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Invoice rejection, rekeying, billing delay, and next-business-day offline submission can matter, and KSeF support volumes show implementation friction. The packet contains no target-segment measurement of those losses or revealed willingness to pay, while a free Ministry mobile app, a 4.99 PLN invoicing offer, existing offline ERP functionality, and the 2026 sanction holiday materially weaken the basis for the proposed 149-699 PLN monthly price.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A monthly or per-reconciled-invoice model has repeat usage, prepayment, and potential software operating leverage. Yet the proposed pricing lacks support against a very low incumbent price anchor, and CAC, retention, onboarding, mapping, failed-submission support, partner share, insurance, security, counsel, and continuing schema-maintenance costs are all unknown, leaving attractive contribution margin and owner earnings speculative.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish installation and mobile-service firms are a legible first segment within a broad mandatory invoicing transition, and the family installation company could provide lawful observational access if it opts in. The packet does not size the exact field-originated invoice segment or its spend, and the smallest firms remain temporarily exempt, so the beachhead is plausible but not yet shown to be economically sufficient.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The Ministry already offers mobile issuance, inFakt offers inexpensive KSeF plumbing, and Comarch Mobile already combines offline issuance with ERP synchronization. The venture owns neither the taxpayer relationship nor the transaction rail, access is nonexclusive and revocable, and no trade-specific capability or channel right is evidenced that could support a dominant position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful proof-to-invoice workflow in one trade could extend to adjacent field-service trades, more accounting packages, and related reconciliation tasks. Each expansion also adds mappings, support load, and KSeF-dependent maintenance, while the packet provides no evidence that the initial advantage would transfer or that adjacent buyers would pay.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Trade templates and a failure-pattern library could improve with use, but there is no evidence that cross-customer pooling is lawful or that such data would outperform official validation rules and incumbent telemetry. Public rules, revocable permissions, nonexclusive integrations, and incumbent installed bases make the proposed advantage easy to copy or bundle away.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Mobile capture, offline issuance, later submission, KSeF handling, and ERP synchronization are already available in the cited alternatives. The potentially valuable differentiation—trade-specific job evidence and cross-accounting-system reconciliation—is only asserted, with no demonstrated improvement in invoice speed, errors, trust, or total cost sufficient to change buyer behavior.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2026 mandatory rollout and potential sanctions from 2027 create a concrete adoption event and recurring compliance need. At the same time, production was reported stable, the 2026 sanction holiday reduces immediate urgency, free support and tools exist, and incumbents have already shipped overlapping solutions, so timing is a mixed catalyst rather than an open window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accounting-office referrals, field-service integrations, and a lawful family-company pilot are credible routes to early learning without a founder-led media brand. No referral or integration agreement, CAC, sales cycle, close rate, or customer relationship is established, while accounting and software incumbents already control trusted channels and can steer customers to bundled alternatives.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-science and automation skills, available capital, and a narrow export-first MVP make technical validation feasible. Production credential security, GDPR, tax-workflow liability, next-day deadline support, fast API changes, insurance, and multiple accounting integrations create a demanding operational surface that is not yet shown to fit a five-hour daily limit alongside full-time employment.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the product from a standalone KSeF transmission bridge to an embedded, export-first proof-to-cash reconciliation module for one installation trade, distributed under contract through an accounting office or vertical field-service platform. Make trade-specific job acceptance, quantities, evidence, and accounting reconciliation—not generic KSeF submission—the paid outcome, and avoid holding customer credentials until demand and support economics are proven.
main_structural_strength: A statutory, high-frequency invoice event can anchor a measurable proof-to-payment workflow, and a narrow trade pilot can be tested with modest capital through lawful founder-adjacent access.
primary_score_limiter: There is no demonstrated trade-specific advantage strong enough to overcome free or cheap substitutes, incumbent distribution, and the taxpayer's revocable control of KSeF permissions.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The core offer is already substantially covered from three directions: a free Ministry mobile app, inFakt's 4.99 PLN KSeF plan, and Comarch Mobile's offline issuance plus ERP synchronization. This directly contradicts an assumption that mobile/offline KSeF plumbing is an underserved, premium-priced wedge.
